do_now: Within the reference band. No action needed.
This reading was not assessed (see the sensor flag). Check contact and measure again.
This value is unusual for you: more than 2 SD from your own 30-day average. Measure again at rest.
tell: Tell the CMO if repeat readings stay unusual.

do_now: Sit and rest 5 minutes, then measure again. If you exercised in the last 10 minutes, rest first.
tell: Tell the CMO if it stays above 90 bpm at rest, or with chest discomfort, dizziness or breathlessness.

do_now: Stop activity, sit or lie down, and measure again with the chest strap or certified oximeter.
tell: Tell the CMO now. The CMO decides whether to contact the flight surgeon.

do_now: Measure again at rest with a certified device. A low resting rate can be normal for trained crew.
tell: Tell the CMO if you feel faint, dizzy or unusually tired.

do_now: Sit or lie down and measure again with a certified device.
tell: Tell the CMO now.

do_now: Warm your hand, keep still and re-measure with the certified oximeter. The sensor value is an estimate.
tell: If the certified reading is 95 % or lower, tell the CMO and check the cabin pressure display.

do_now: Keep still, stop activity if short of breath, and confirm with the certified oximeter now.
tell: If confirmed, tell the CMO now; the CMO contacts the flight surgeon.

do_now: Re-measure with the clinical thermometer. Add a layer and check the cabin temperature.
tell: Tell the CMO if it stays below 36.1 °C or you are shivering.

do_now: Warm up now: add layers and move to a warmer module. Re-measure in 15 minutes.
tell: Tell the CMO now.

do_now: Rest away from exercise and heat, and re-measure with the clinical thermometer in 15 minutes.
tell: Tell the CMO and answer the symptom check.

do_now: Sit quietly 5 minutes, arm supported at heart level, then take two readings 1 minute apart and enter both. Single reading is a screening prompt.
tell: Tell the CMO at the next check-in if readings stay at 130/80 or above on two different days.

do_now: Sit quietly 5 minutes, arm supported at heart level, then take two readings 1 minute apart and enter both. Single reading is a screening prompt.
tell: Tell the CMO at the next check-in if readings stay at 130/80 or above on two different days.

do_now: Sit quietly and measure again after 5 minutes. Single reading is a screening prompt.
tell: If still above 180/120, tell the CMO now; the CMO contacts the flight surgeon.

do_now: Sit quietly and measure again after 5 minutes. Single reading is a screening prompt.
tell: If still above 180/120, tell the CMO now; the CMO contacts the flight surgeon.

do_now: Sit or lie down and measure again. Stand up slowly.
tell: Tell the CMO if you feel light-headed or faint.

do_now: Lie down with your legs raised and measure again.
tell: Tell the CMO now.

do_now: Follow the low-glucose step in the crew medical checklist and re-measure in 15 minutes. Screening prompt only.
tell: Tell the CMO if it stays below 70 mg/dL.

do_now: Stop activity, follow the low-glucose step in the crew medical checklist now, and do not exercise alone.
tell: Tell the CMO now.

do_now: Note what and when you last ate, and measure again before your next meal. Screening prompt only; timing unknown.
tell: Tell the CMO at the next check-in if repeat readings stay at 140 mg/dL or above.

do_now: Wash and dry your hands and re-measure with a fresh strip. Screening prompt only.
tell: If still 200 mg/dL or above, tell the CMO now.

do_now: Plan a sleep period of at least 7 hours tonight and dim the module lights before it.
tell: Tell the CMO if short nights continue; they reduce alertness on critical tasks.

do_now: Your 7-day average is under 7 hours. Protect the sleep period in tomorrow's schedule.
tell: Review the schedule with the CMO.

do_now: Take a short break and talk with a crewmate you trust.
tell: If low mood continues or affects your work, tell the CMO; private time with ground support can be requested.

do_now: Mood has been low for a week. Talk with a crewmate or request private time with ground support.
tell: Tell the CMO at the next check-in.

do_now: Check the CO2 scrubber status and the fans, and move to a module with better airflow.
tell: Tell the CMO and answer the headache check.

do_now: The 7-day CO2 average is above 2.5 mmHg, where headache reports rise. Check ventilation.
tell: Tell the CMO at the next check-in; report headaches in the symptom check.

do_now: The cabin temperature is outside the bounding box of NASA's crew health limits. Check the thermal control setpoint and fans.
tell: Tell the CMO.

do_now: The cabin humidity is outside NASA's crew health limits. Check the humidity control and fans.
tell: Tell the CMO.

do_now: The temperature is outside the zone where crew perform best. Adjust the setpoint and check the fans.
The humidity is outside the zone where crew perform best. Check the humidity control.
Work-surface light is below 350 lx. Turn up the work lights while awake.
Half of the career dose limit is used. No immediate action.
tell: Review planned EVAs with the CMO at the next check-in.

do_now: You are near the career dose limit. Avoid optional EVAs until reviewed.
tell: Tell the CMO; the flight surgeon reviews remaining exposure.

do_now: Space weather is elevated: a strong flare or geomagnetic storm in the last 24 hours. Check that the shelter route is clear.
tell: Tell the CMO at the next check-in.

do_now: Solar particle event alert. Go to the designated shelter area and stay until the all-clear.
tell: Acknowledge with your badge or the console button; the CMO informs the flight surgeon.

why: Heart rate at rest is a basic sign of how the heart is coping. Spaceflight changes the cardiovascular system, so a trend helps the CMO spot a problem early.
Fluids shift toward the head in space, which can change blood pressure. A regular reading shows a trend early, so the CMO can act first.
Fluids shift toward the head in space, which can change blood pressure. A regular reading shows a trend early, so the CMO can act first.
Glucose reflects how the body gets and uses fuel. Food supply in flight is constrained, so a trend can flag a nutrition problem early.
Body temperature is a basic sign that something may be wrong. A steady rise or fall tells the CMO when to look closer.
Crews often sleep less in flight, and sleep loss lowers alertness and performance. Logging it lets the crew change the schedule early.
Mood is an early sign of how the crew copes with isolation and confinement. A low trend is a prompt to talk and ask for support.

do_now: Check that every meal and drink was logged, and that logged items report sodium. Logged totals may be incomplete.
tell: Tell the CMO at the next check-in if the total stays above the NASA reference range.

tell: Tell the CMO now if the total is confirmed.

tell: Tell the CMO now if the total is confirmed.
